Hi all — quick technical breakdown of what Redwood can provide today and what requires an ops engagement:

1) Residency / locality guarantees (standard):
- For Private/VPC deployments we pin all customer data storage and inference workloads to the customer's chosen region. Storage buckets and object stores are provisioned in that region.
- Network egress is routable only via customer-specified subnets and NAT gateways when deployed in a VPC; control plane operations are configurable to use regional endpoints.

Artifacts we can provide out of the box:
- Object-store manifests (list of keys/objects with timestamps and size) exported as CSV.
- Server-side logs showing instance IDs, AZ/region identifiers, and request timestamps for a given time-window. Logs include signed digests.

2) Deletion evidence (options):
- Standard: deletion manifest (objects marked deleted + deletion timestamp), with S3-style delete markers.
- Enhanced: cryptographic hash manifest (SHA256 per object) + signed attestation from our control plane (RSA signature) stating that deletion occurred at X time and objects are no longer addressable.
- For snapshots or DB backups we can provide a snapshot manifest and a deletion event with a tamper-evident signature.

3) Keys & attestation: BYOK vs Redwood KMS
- BYOK: we support customer-provided KMS keys (cloud KMS or externally managed HSM). In BYOK mode, Redwood cannot decrypt objects without customer authorization; we can still produce metadata and manifests, but hashes of encrypted payloads are provided.
- HSM-backed signing: we can support a Redwood-controlled signing HSM for attestations, or integrate with customer HSM to sign attestations (requires key-sharing/trust setup and an ops run).

4) Turnaround time & cost
- Standard exports (manifests + logs for a 30-day window): 48 business hours, no charge for active customers on Dedicated/Dedicated+ support tier.
- Enhanced authenticated attestations (signed hashes, HSM-signed statements): 3-5 business days; PO/ops fee applies.
- Emergency/legal requests: expedited within 24 hours with an emergency SOW.

5) Practical caveats:
- If the customer uses their own cross-region replication or external backup targets, we cannot attest to those copies.
- For air-gapped on-prem deployments, evidence flows are local — we can provide the same manifests but signing requires a previously-agreed key-exchange.

I'll attach a sample CSV manifest and a short template for the acceptance criteria. Happy to jump on a quick call with Claire to walk through examples.

- Ben

Thanks Ben — adding the commercial / acceptance template notes. Claire, one thing from procurement/legal side:

- We maintain an acceptance template that maps each customer requirement to an "evidence artifact" we can provide (manifest, log slice, signed attestation). I've attached the template (residency_acceptance_template_v1.docx).
- Suggested approach: mediscn sync signs the template with checkboxes for the minimum artifacts required. We then propose a 30-day pilot window where Redwood demonstrates the artifacts for a sample 7-day window.
- Cost note: the pilot/demo artifacts are covered at no charge. If Medisync requests ad-hoc enhanced attestations on an ongoing cadence (monthly signed attestations, full historical proofs), we typically put those under a modest evidence-retention addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Claire reviews the attached template and ticks required artifacts.
2) We schedule a 45-minute call (technical demo + sample manifest walkthrough).
3) Post-demo, if Medisync requires HSM-signed attestations we scope an ops runbook and SOW.

Timeline estimate: 7-10 business days to set up demo artifacts and 3-5 days to produce an enhanced attestation after SOW approval.

Cheers,

Claire — consolidating our responses and proposed ops path below. Please see attached sample manifest and the acceptance template.

What Redwood can provide immediately (no extra SOW):
- Region-pinned object storage and audit logs scoped to your VPC.
- Exportable object-store manifests (CSV) and server logs with region metadata.
- Standard deletion manifest (timestamps and delete markers) within 48 business hours.

What requires an ops runbook / SOW:
- HSM-backed attestations or customer-key signing of attestations (we need a key-exchange and validation run).
- Regular scheduled signed attestations (monthly/quarterly) for historical windows — can be added to a support/retention addendum.

Proposed next steps (operational path):
1) Claire reviews and ticks the attached residency_acceptance_template_v1.docx and returns it to procurement@redwood.ai.
2) We set up a 45-minute technical demo (Ben) to walk Medisync security through the sample manifest and the control-plane attestations.
3) If Medisync needs HSM-signed attestations, Redwood will draft an ops runbook and SOW; timeline 3-5 business days after sign-off.

Deliverables attached to kick off the pilot:
- residency_acceptance_template_v1.docx
- s3_manifest_sample.csv

If this looks good I'll book the demo for next week. Thanks again for the clear asks — we'll get this into the acceptance checklist so procurement can move forward.
